current.text: He signed with Brooklyn as veteran depth on a 2-year, 18 million deal with a mutual option.
The newest call expects Ellis, not the rookie Mikel Brown Jr., to start for the Nets. Earlier Nets previews had Brown starting and Ellis as the likely sixth man.
He needs about 27 minutes a game to matter in 12-team category leagues. At that load he is a later-round flyer. Below it, treat him as a stash, not a must-roster, and do not target him aggressively.
Brooklyn projects as one of the worst teams, at about 28 wins. Its pick goes to Houston, so it has no reason to tank.
Minutes in the second half of the season are uncertain. Brooklyn could shift minutes to young players such as Brown, Demin, Minott and Clowney, which could cut into a veteran depth role.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league. With our March 28 end, its playoff schedule is 3-4-3 games, with one back-to-back in the playoff weeks.

durable.text: His category value comes from steals and very few turnovers. He gives little in points, rebounds and assists.

note: Both sites give Ellis 0 USD of value, at rank 260 on Yahoo and 195 on ESPN. That puts him well outside the 144 players we draft, so leave him on waivers on draft day. In that case his steals and very low turnovers fit a team that already has its points, rebounds and assists. Check the Nets' starting lineup and his minutes in the first two weeks.
